business_problem: IBM wanted to help developers understand undocumented code, generate documentation faster and reduce the manual effort required to work across large, inherited codebases.
solution_summary: IBM teams used IBM watsonx Code Assistant during the watsonx Challenge to speed up code explanation, documentation, generation and test creation across large, inherited repositories. One highlighted team had taken over more than 50 undocumented code repositories containing about 750 JavaScript files and used the assistant to summarize large files, explain advanced syntax and generate scripts that identified which files still needed documentation. In the working pattern, developers submit source files or natural-language prompts to the assistant, review the generated outputs and then incorporate accurate summaries or generated code into their maintenance workflow. Because watsonx Code Assistant is embedded directly in development tasks, it reduces the time needed to understand legacy code, document APIs and onboard newer engineers without requiring every contributor to be a deep expert in the codebase.
